findings.text: dict(row) is a shallow copy, so the row's nested values, the commits and changed_paths lists and any nested mapping, are shared with the cache entry and with every other caller's row, and a caller that mutates a nested value corrupts the process-wide reuse for every later read while the docstring that opens at ledger.py:1329 says the reuse is never handed out.

the timing probe reads entry.tottime, an attribute the profiler entry does not carry, so both arms crashed in the node's own scaffolding right after the first roadmap call returned ok=False and never reached the second call's timing or the crew runs-view timing, which means the missing done-when figure is partly an instrument defect.

the landing fragment's plan-verdict meta says passed while its own prose records the warm-read timing and decode share as not obtained, so a reader who scans verdicts reads a pass on the clause carrying the section's headline claim.

the module already exceeded the worker-window bound at base, 51,665 estimated tokens against a 50,000 bound, and the added lines take it to 52,456, deepening the repo-wide failure of tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py that this node's own gate carries, though the plan's write paths sanction extending this file.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base 33158f8b9; 6b4f1aa82 is the decode reuse in reckon/ledger.py, 70d7ad6c7 is the 28-line landing fragment, and the 86 added lines of reckon/ledger.py are the whole change.
item_verdicts.done_when: read at the reviewed run's prompt.txt FENCE-EVIDENCE; it names the seven-file gate, the two decode-count conditions and the base/head warm-roadmap timing with its cProfile decode share; the recorded gate logs hold the first two and the third has no figure, both arms' timing logs ending in the probe's own AttributeError instead.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is to reuse decoded run-ledger payloads within a process so a warm ledger.load decodes an unchanged index once; reckon/ledger.py:1295 _decoded_payload holds each decoded row against the index's own stored stamp and reckon/ledger.py:1316 _index_payload consumes it, so what landed is the deliverable section 45 states.
item_verdicts.manifest: read at the run directory; it records the three-test file at 3 passed EXIT=0, the head gate at 1 failed 118 passed against base 1 failed 115 passed with the same single failing id, the decode counts 8 then 0 then 1, and the timing clause under follow_ons and blockers rather than as a figure.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the four declared paths are reckon/ledger.py, tests/test_a_warm_ledger_load_decodes_once.py, docs/evidence/fragments/a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline/a-warm-ledger-load-decodes-once.html and a figures directory; all three paths in the diff (git diff --stat 33158f8b9 70d7ad6c7) are inside them and the figures directory is unused.

justifications.durability: the declared negative control at negative-control.log reinstates the regression by replacing ledger._decoded_payload with a pass-through and all three tests fail with EXIT=1, so the assertions do guard the change; the copies property is asserted only for a top-level key at tests/test_a_warm_ledger_load_decodes_once.py:126.
justifications.evidence: the gate the done_when names ran and is logged at gate-head.log and gate-base.log with their EXIT lines, but the done_when's third clause, the base and head warm-roadmap timing with its decode share against the 1.33 s figure, has no figure in any log.
justifications.fit: the addition follows the module's own identity-keyed cache at reckon/ledger.py:2715 and its stamp-keyed lru_cache at reckon/ledger.py:222, and introduces no name the repository's naming rules forbid.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/ledger.py:1355 and 1369 route every aggregate row and every record row through _decoded_payload, so a warm load over an unchanged index re-parses nothing, which is what the goal states.
justifications.reuse: the search of reckon/ledger.py for an existing decoded-payload reuse found _INDEX_REGION at ledger.py:1444, a region-scoped whole-read reuse, _identity_catalogue at ledger.py:222 and _RESOLVED_FLIGHT_CACHE at ledger.py:2715, none of which owns per-payload decode reuse, so this extends the module's stamp-keyed-reuse idiom rather than duplicating an owner.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff, reckon/ledger.py, tests/test_a_warm_ledger_load_decodes_once.py and the plan evidence fragment, is inside the declared four, and nothing else was touched.
